neighbours.label: Function words that frame a definition, assumption or condition in mathematical exposition ('often called', 'note that', 'provided that', 'whether'), vs the same framing words in everyday prose
fire: In group theory, such mappings are often called homomorphisms.
We say the matrix is invertible; note that this requires a nonzero determinant.
The bound holds provided that the function is continuous on the interval.
It remains open whether every even number is the sum of two primes.
In topology, these sets are often called neighbourhoods of the point.
Note that the integral is taken over the closed unit disc.
The estimate is sharp provided that p is greater than one.
One must check whether the sequence is bounded before taking limits.
quiet: In our village, such markets are often called fairs.
We say the shop is closed; note that this happens on public holidays.
The picnic goes ahead provided that it does not rain on Sunday.
It remains unclear whether every guest will arrive on time.
In our town, these lanes are often called alleys by the locals.
Note that the parking is free on the first Sunday of the month.
The trip is cheap provided that you book three weeks ahead.
One must check whether the oven is hot before baking bread.
